value: In this lesson, we're going to learn how to read BIG words — words with two beats!
But first, let's review some of the letters, sounds, and words we learned in previous lessons.
Remember clapping word beats? ‘Camping’ has two beats: CAMP-ING.
Big words are just small chunks holding hands! Today we learn to read them one beat at a time.
We'll climb three rungs of a ladder, from easiest to trickiest.
Rung one: some big words are just two little words stuck together!
‘Sun’ + ‘set’ = ‘sunset’. ‘Hot’ + ‘dog’ = ‘hotdog’.
Read the first little word, read the second little word, then say them together.
Read each word one beat at a time, then say the whole word.

value.value: Have {name} cover the second half with a finger, read the first word, then reveal and read the rest.

value: Rung two: some big words start with a little chunk that has a meaning.
‘un-’ means NOT or the opposite: ‘undo’ means to do the opposite of do. ‘Unzip’!
‘re-’ means AGAIN: ‘redo’ means do it again. ‘Retell’ means tell it again!
Read the chunk, read the rest, then say the whole word.
Rung three: the trickiest! Some big words need to be split in the middle.
Find the vowels, split between the two consonants in the middle, read each chunk, then join them.
‘Rabbit’ splits into rab-bit. ‘Napkin’ splits into nap-kin.

value.value: Cover one half at a time to help {name} read each chunk before joining them.

value: Split each word in the middle, read each chunk, then join the chunks.
One new heart word today, and it's a big one: ‘people’.
You'll see it everywhere. It doesn't follow the rules at all, so we learn it by heart.
